name: PyFloat_GetMax
reason: FloatInfoCorrect proves every finite F64 has abs value at most PyFloat_GetMax, which no other constant satisfies (toRat of an infinity is 0), so DBL_MAX ("maximum representable finite float", :54) is pinned exactly.

name: PyFloat_GetMin
reason: FloatInfoCorrect pins GetMin as the encoding with biased exponent 1 and zero fraction, value 2**-1022, the smallest positive normal that the DBL_MIN field doc (:59) promises.

name: PyFloat_GetInfo
reason: FloatInfoCorrect pins max, min, epsilon, mant_dig, max_exp and min_exp but never max_10_exp, min_10_exp, dig, radix or rounds (:108, :111, :112, :115, :116), so a GetInfo with dig = 16 or rounds = 0 passes.

name: PyFloat_FromDouble
reason: no-behaviour applies: the body only takes a freelist slot or mallocs and stores fval, and its MemoryError is allocator plumbing.

name: float_from_string_inner
reason: FloatBlankRaises only states that empty or all-space input raises ValueError, so an inner that raises ValueError for every string passes; the value of float(s) for a real numeral, the trailing-whitespace strip (:156-159) and the end != last check (:165) are never stated.

name: PyFloat_FromString
reason: StrArg has no shape for a non-string, non-buffer argument, so the TypeError at :216-220 is not modelled, and FloatBlankRaises pins only blank strings, so a version raising ValueError for every str and bytes passes.

name: _PyFloat_ExactDealloc
reason: no-behaviour applies: the body only returns the object to the float freelist.

name: float_dealloc
reason: no-behaviour applies: the body only frees the object (freelist or tp_free) and is a tp_dealloc that drops nothing visible, per the finalization policy.

name: PyFloat_AsDouble
reason: Obj.other carries __float__ and __index__ results as plain values, so __float__ raising (:278-281), __index__ raising or returning a non-int (:265-268), and the DeprecationWarning turned into an error for a float-subclass result (:290-297) cannot be expressed, though FloatAsDouble pins every branch the model does have.

name: _Py_convert_int_to_double
reason: IntToFloatCorrect pins PyLong_AsDouble and convertToDouble (.int n) only below the overflow limit, so a version returning ok inf on overflow (instead of the error at :325-329) or raising for a non-int (instead of NotImplemented at :331-334) passes.

name: float_repr
reason: ReprSpecial pins only NaNs, infinities and zeros, so a repr returning '0.0' for every other finite float passes; the round-trip entry float-repr-roundtrip that would pin finite values is open.

name: float_richcompare
reason: FloatIntCompareExact pins the int branch exactly for all six operators and every int, but the float-vs-float branch (:383-384 then Compare) and the NotImplemented exits (:394, :504-505) are unstated, so a version answering false for every finite float pair (1.0 < 2.0 included) passes (typeobj-nan-never-equal adds only NaN == and !=).

name: float_hash
reason: FloatHashBasics pins infinities, NaN-by-identity, never -1 and hash(0.0) == hash(-0.0), so a version hashing every finite float to 0 passes; the exact modular rule (float-hash-numeric-tower) is open.

name: float_add
reason: FloatAddCorrect pins only two finite float operands, so a version returning 0.0 for inf + 1.0 or for inf + -inf, or NotImplemented for an int operand (where CONVERT_TO_DOUBLE converts it or raises OverflowError for 10**400), passes.

name: float_sub
reason: FloatSubCorrect pins only two finite float operands; infinities and NaNs, int operands and their OverflowError, and NotImplemented for other types are unconstrained.

name: float_mul
reason: FloatMulCorrect pins only two finite float operands; inf * 0.0, other non-finite operands, int operands with their OverflowError, and NotImplemented are unconstrained.

name: float_div
reason: FloatDivCorrect pins the zero-divisor error for every float x and finite / nonzero finite, but inf / 2.0, nan / 1.0, x / inf, int operands with their OverflowError and NotImplemented are unconstrained.

name: float_rem
reason: DivmodTwins and DivmodZero pin float_rem on two float operands (equal to divmod's remainder, ZeroDivisionError for zero), but never with an int operand or a non-number, so a version returning NotImplemented for 7.5 % 2 or not raising OverflowError for 1.0 % 10**400 passes, and no statement fixes the remainder itself (sign of wx, abs below abs(wx)) other than by its twin.

name: _float_div_mod
reason: The remainder is pinned to float_rem's independent copy of the same logic by DivmodTwins over all float pairs, NaNs and infinities included, and the quotient is settled by two refutations (exact floor, and the divmod doc's floor-or-one-less) whose counterexamples run this mirror and reproduce on 3.15.2 (bugs/binary64-floordiv-not-exact-floor.yaml).

name: float_divmod
reason: DivmodZero and DivmodTwins determine it on two float operands, but the int-operand conversion with its OverflowError and the NotImplemented exit are never stated, and the quotient refutations are stated on float_div_mod, not on float_divmod.

name: float_floor_div
reason: DivmodZero and DivmodTwins determine it on two float operands, but the int-operand conversion (1e308 // 10**400 raises OverflowError) and the NotImplemented exit are never stated, and FloorDivExactFloor runs float_div_mod, not this wrapper.

name: float_pow
reason: PowSpecialValues covers w == 0, v == 1, a NaN base, zero to a negative finite power, negative base with a fractional exponent and the positive-finite cpow call, but not v**nan (:708-710), the isinf(iw) branch (:711-725), the isinf(iv) branch with the odd-integer sign (:726-737), the sign of 0.0**w (:747-748), or negate_result for a negative base with an integer exponent (:765-766, :781, :791-792), so a version giving (-2.0)**3 == 8.0 or 0.5**inf == inf passes; the errno model also drops any errno pow sets on a finite result (:794-800).

name: float_neg
reason: FloatUnary states only that neg is an involution that flips the sign, so a neg that also flips the lowest fraction bit passes; the entry's claim "flips only the sign bit" is not what the prop says (it lacks bexp and frac equality as stated for abs).

name: float_abs
reason: FloatUnary fixes sign, biased exponent and fraction of abs(x) for every F64, which determines all 64 bits of fabs.

name: float_bool
reason: FloatUnary: bool(x) is false exactly for the two zeros, over every F64 (NaNs are true, as v != 0.0 gives).

name: float_is_integer_impl
reason: FloatIsInteger: true exactly for finite floats with an integer value, over every F64; the errno branch after floor (:845-851) is unreachable on IEEE floor.

name: float___trunc___impl
reason: FloatIntConversions pins truncation toward zero for finite x, ValueError for NaN and OverflowError for infinities with PyLong_FromDouble's messages (longobject.c:490-498).

name: float___floor___impl
reason: FloatIntConversions pins the exact floor for finite x and the NaN/infinity errors in PyLong_FromDouble's order.

name: float___ceil___impl
reason: FloatIntConversions pins the exact ceiling for finite x and the NaN/infinity errors.

name: double_round
reason: The platform note is wrong: this is the _PY_SHORT_FLOAT_REPR == 1 version (#if at :901), the one every IEEE build compiles (pycore_pymath.h:197), and the registry already models it (Dtoa.lean double_round, entry float-round-extremes); the row should be modelled, and float-round-extremes pins only zeros for it.

name: double_round
reason: platform applies: the fallback sits in the #else of _PY_SHORT_FLOAT_REPR == 1 (:958-1008), compiled only without correctly rounded dtoa.

name: float___round___impl
reason: The model takes ndigits as an Int, so the TypeError or __index__ failure of PyNumber_AsSsize_t (:1042-1044) is not modelled, and FloatRoundExtremes pins only non-finite x, n > 323, n < -308 and zeros, so round(x) (float-round-half-even, open) and the correctly rounded double_round path for ordinary x and n are unconstrained.

name: float_float
reason: The model is the identity on F64, which erases the two branches (the same object for an exact float, a new exact float from a subclass, :1071-1076), and FloatIdentities proves it by rfl on a one-line definition.

name: float_conjugate_impl
reason: Defined as float_float, so it inherits the collapsed exact/subclass branches, and FloatIdentities proves x = x by rfl.

name: char_from_hex

name: hex_from_char

name: float_hex_impl
reason: FloatHexSign only relates (-x).hex() to x.hex() for positive finite x, so a hex returning 'a' for every positive float passes; the digits, exponent and subnormal shift are unconstrained (float-hex-roundtrip is open), and NaN, infinity and zero outputs are not stated.

name: float_fromhex_impl
reason: The mirror stops at :1443: the subclass call PyObject_CallOneArg(type, result) (:1444-1446) and the PyUnicode_AsUTF8AndSize failure for non-str or surrogate input (:1280-1282) are not modelled; the refutation itself ('1p2000x' raises OverflowError) is sound and reproduced.

name: float_as_integer_ratio_impl

name: float_new_impl

name: float_subtype_new

name: float_vectorcall

name: float_from_number_impl
reason: The model is PyFloat_AsDouble alone, missing the exact-float identity return (:1644-1647) and the subclass call PyObject_CallOneArg(type, result) (:1653-1655), and FloatIdentities states only a float argument, so the TypeError for a str is never stated.

name: float___getnewargs___impl

name: float___getformat___impl
reason: GetFormat determines it for every string: 'IEEE, little-endian' for 'double' and 'float' and the exact ValueError otherwise, for the little-endian hosts the model states as its scope.

name: float_getreal
reason: Defined as float_float, so it inherits the collapsed exact/subclass branches, and FloatIdentities proves x = x by rfl.

name: float_getimag

name: PyFloat_Pack4

name: PyFloat_Pack8

name: PyFloat_Unpack4

name: PyFloat_Unpack8
reason: Pack8RoundTrip gives Unpack8 (layout 8 x.bits le) le = x for every F64 and both byte orders, and layout 8 covers every 8-byte input, so Unpack8 is determined on all of them.
